st_habitudes.name: Rue des Vieilles-Baskets
st_habitudes.alt: A grassy hillside garden where stone steps climb between ivy-covered banks toward a little gazebo at the top, with an old street lamp, a big tree and four round painted doors set into the slope: yellow, red, blue and, highest up, green. Monsieur Verbe hugs a puppy he has just lifted out of a basket; drops an apple into a crate with a grimace; picks up the old wall telephone; tucks into a chocolate cake at a little table; stares as his pink ice cream melts, in a purple beret; and holds up his old trainer full of holes. The path on the left leads back down to the houses.

doors.label: Ruelle des Chaussons

chaussons.name: Ruelle des Chaussons
chaussons.alt: A sunny lawn on a landing of the garden steps, walled in by a tall hedge, with an old iron pump and bucket, a little round table with a checkerboard and a gray cat, a wooden bench and flower beds: Monsieur Verbe whistles with his back turned while the pump overflows the bucket; kneels to stroke a happy dog; sneaks a checker across the board while the cat looks away; pulls on a green welly on the bench; scrunches a sheet of paper into a ball; and unfolds a big map. The yellow door in the wall leads back.

herons.name: Allée des Hérons
herons.alt: A landing of the garden steps beside a lily pond where a gray heron stands, with a big tree hung with a lantern and steps climbing to a cozy guest cottage with a bed inside: Monsieur Verbe slumps on a step, tongue out and exhausted; spreads his arms wide beside the heron spreading its wings; trips on a stone in a gold beret; cheers a tortoise up the steps with red pom-poms; dangles from the tree branch by the lantern in a purple beret; and carries an old lady's suitcase toward the guest cottage. The red door in the wall leads back.

affiches.name: Rue des Affiches
affiches.alt: A vegetable terrace on the garden hillside beside the stone steps, with rows of carrots, a wooden potting shed, a little iron stove with a copper kettle, a notice board and a goat: Monsieur Verbe heaves a giant carrot out of the ground; scolds the goat, red in the face, as it chews a poster; sets a striped barrier across the steps; puts the kettle on the stove; heads back down the steps with his basket in a purple beret; and pins a cat poster on the notice board. The blue door in the wall leads back.

veilleurs.name: Rue des Veilleurs-de-Nuit
veilleurs.alt: The top of the garden steps at night under a full moon, with a wooden summerhouse glowing with a lantern, a kitten asleep in an old armchair, an iron pump and a little table with a glass pitcher: Monsieur Verbe rushes toward a puppy in a gold beret; carries a little bed into the summerhouse; holds up a present wrapped in spotty paper; sits up awake by the lantern keeping watch; tips green ink into the clear pitcher of water; and rinses carrots under the pump. The green door in the wall leads back.
